in_text_mentions: nflammatory dermatoses. There was no parental consanguinity and no history of miscarriages. On examination, there was erythroderma, generalized thick adherent scale in a feathery pattern following lines of Blaschko, and shiny red whorls on the dorsolateral feet (Figure 1A–1F). There was no skin peeling or skin fragility. Several fingernails were hypoplastic. The nasal bridge was flat, and the neck was short. Red reflexes were present bilaterally, but both eyes were noted to be small. The head and trunk were large relative to the limbs, and the proximal limb segments were proportionately short.

Panel A caption states small and narrow thorax; image also shows punctate calcifications consistent with stippled epiphyseal calcification vocabulary term. B: Same fetus X-ray, captioned short limbs with article in-text asymmetric short limbs. Maps to asymmetric limb shortening in CDPX2. In addition, the shapes of T3 to L3 were abnormal, the vertebral bodies appeared fused, the thorax was small with a maximum circumference of 16 cm, and the abdominal circumference was 26 cm. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Newborn photograph showing the characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism (flat facial profile, collapsed nasal bridge, protruding forehead) described in the caption and in-text for a confirmed EBP-mutation CDPX2 case; these features are not in the provided findings vocabulary and are listed as proposed findings. B: Clinical photograph of the neonate's back showing generalized erythematous scaly ichthyosiform skin, matching the caption's 'congenital ichthyosis' in a confirmed CDPX2 case; classic presenting feature of CHHS. C: Clinical photograph of the scalp showing patchy hair loss/alopecia as stated in the caption, corresponding to cicatricial alopecia of scalp, a recognized classic cutaneous feature of CHHS.

in_text_mentions: After birth, physical examination showed a collapsed nasal bridge, protruding forehead, flat facial profile, congenital ichthyosis and alopecia. It is worth noting that there is no syndactyly of the fourth and fifth fingers of the proband’s left hand. The initial appearance may have been due to the angle of the image (Fig. 1). Respiratory assessment indicated shortness of breath with inspiratory retraction, requiring continuos positive airway pressure support. Thoracic deformities were not observed. Limb examination revealed short limbs with slightly increased muscle tension.

plate_findings.evidence: Skin biopsies from linear scaly streaks showed orthohyperkeratosis (Figure 2A, 100× H&E)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of the CHHS patient's biopsy showing orthohyperkeratosis and dilated keratin-plugged follicular ostia, corresponding to the clinically sampled Blaschko-linear scaly streaks. B: High-power H&E confirming the same ichthyosiform follicular changes in the CHHS newborn's biopsy. C: Von Kossa stain demonstrating calcification within corneocytes and follicles in the same CHHS patient's biopsy; a reported histologic clue in CHHS ichthyosiform skin. D: Lower-power von Kossa view confirming follicular and stratum corneum calcification in CHHS patient tissue.
panels.attribution_text: O'Connor et al. Early Skin Biopsy in Conradi-Hünermann-Happle Syndrome (X-Linked Dominant Chondrodysplasia Punctata).. Journal of cutaneous pathology 2025. doi:10.1111/cup.14837. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology of skin biopsies showing orthohyperkeratosis and numerous dilated follicular ostia with keratin plugs on low power (Figure 2A, 100× H&E) and high power (Figure 2B, 200× H&E); and foci of calcification in the corneocytes of the stratum corneum and hair follicles, highlighted with a von Kossa stain (Figure 2C, 200× von Kossa, and Figure 2D, 100× von Kossa).
in_text_mentions: of signs, CHHS was suspected clinically. Skin biopsies in the first 12 h of life from linear scaly streaks showed orthohyperkeratosis and numerous dilated follicular ostia with keratin plugs (Figure 2A–2B). Foci of calcification were seen in the corneocytes of the stratum corneum and hair follicles, highlighted with a von Kossa stain (Figure 2C–2D). Skeletal survey showed symmetric punctate calcification/stippling of the proximal femoral epiphysis and ankle bilaterally and of the right humeral epiphysis and right carpus, in keeping with chondrodysplasia punctata, although no gross rhizomelia

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'bending and short femur (arrows), thick metaphysis with high echoes (arrowheads)'; in-text: 'thick metaphysis in the right lower limb'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Prenatal ultrasound of the affected fetus at 24+5 weeks showing the narrow/small thorax (arrowhead) and shortened spine (arrow) described in the caption; these are recognized skeletal manifestations in the severe CHHS fetal phenotype, but no vocab finding_key maps directly to them. B: Fetal ultrasound showing short, bent femur with hyperechoic thickened metaphysis; the unilateral (right lower limb) involvement supports the asymmetric limb shortening characteristic of Conradi-Hünermann-Happle syndrome in this confirmed X-linked dominant chondrodysplasia punctata fetus. C: Prenatal facial profile ultrasound of the same affected fetus showing flat face and flattened nasal bridge per caption; a recognized dysmorphic feature of the severe CHHS phenotype, though no matching finding_key exists in the vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Liu et al. X-linked dominant chondrodysplasia punctata with severe phenotype in a female fetus: A case report.. Medicine 2019. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000013850. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound findings: (A) at gestational week 24+5: small and narrow thorax (arrowhead), chest circumference 15.6 cm, abdominal circumference 21.1 cm, shorter spine (arrow); (B) at gestational week 24+5: bending and short femur (arrows), thick metaphysis with high echoes (arrowheads); and (C) flat face and nose bridge (arrows).
in_text_mentions: served, with no positive findings. Non-invasive DNA analysis showed low trisomy 21 risk, low trisomy 18 risk, and low trisomy 13 risk. At gestational week 24+5, ultrasound examination showed abnormal development of the long bones of the limbs (the length of the long bones was shorter than 1% controlled to the same gestational week of normal fetus), thick metaphysis in the right lower limb, irregular vertebral arrangement, and a narrow and small thorax (Fig. 1 A–D). The patient's parents decided to terminate the pregnancy at 27 weeks of gestation considering this as a lethal skeletal dysplasia.

panels.rationale: The figure is a spine radiograph explicitly showing epiphysial calcifications and vertebral dysmorphisms as mentioned in the caption, strongly supporting a diagnosis of Conradi-Hünermann-Happle Syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Hatia et al. Chondrodysplasia Punctata: Early Diagnosis and Multidisciplinary Management of Conradi-Hünermann-Happle Syndrome (CDPX2).. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.75605. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Spine radiography of the patient. The image shows calcifications of the epiphyseal cartilages in the anterior costal arches and the vertebral column (stars), scoliosis (arrow), and vertebral dysmorphisms, such as reduced height of vertebral bodies and rounded morphology of vertebral bodies at the dorsolumbar level (squares).
in_text_mentions: A simple X-ray of the skeleton revealed calcifications in many of the epiphyseal cartilages of the axial and appendicular skeletons, especially near the anterior costal arches and the vertebral column. The patient presented with dysmorphic ribs ("oar-shaped ribs"), spinal dysraphism at C4, scoliosis, and vertebral dysmorphisms, such as reduced vertebral body height, hemivertebra at D9, and rounded morphology of some vertebral bodies at the dorsolumbar level (Figure 1).
